reasons: Classification is correct: Article VIX provides the Licensed Technology wholly 'AS IS' and disclaims all warranties 'WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED', including any nonconformity-to-Documentation correction, and no affirmative conformance warranty exists elsewhere (only a 'commercially reasonable efforts' Error Correction covenant with no remedy). That is the playbook's walk-away position, so it fails the 90-day/30-day fallback and a redline is warranted.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it carves the express warranties out of the disclaimer (removing 'WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND' and 'WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED', limiting the disclaimer to 'ALL OTHER IMPLIED WARRANTIES') and inserts a conformance warranty (12 months), workmanlike performance, legal compliance and no-malicious-code, with repair/replace and a refund backstop — matching the model language and reaching the preferred position.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic on p0110 (ratio 0.662) is expected here: the rule expressly requires rewriting the AS IS/blanket-disclaimer sentence to carve out express warranties, and the edit is confined to the words that must change.

The residual negations in p0113/p0115 ('does not warrant ... nonconformity to its Documentation can or will be corrected') are neutralized by the 'EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE' carve-out and the 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' preamble, so the disclaimer no longer swallows the new warranty.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the 90-day/30-day fallback. Minor drafting nit only (not a basis to reject): clause (b) references 'Specifications', which may not be a defined term in this Agreement — consider limiting it to the Documentation.
